properties.description:

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

Animas River.

- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.

to fall below flood stage overnight.

through flooded areas.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

San Juan River At Farmington affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Farmington.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 8.5 feet, Overbank flow is occurring from just below
the confluence of the Animas and San Juan Rivers at Farmington, and
continuing downriver through Shiprock. At this water level, the
fast flow can result in river bank erosion but otherwise minor
flood damage.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- There is no current observed data. The river has crested and will
generally continue to fall through Sunday.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will fall to near flood stage just after
midnight tonight. It will then rise to 9.2 feet early Sunday
morning. It will then fall below flood stage around mid day
Sunday.
- Flood stage is 8.5 feet.
- The San Juan River at Farmington has crested at an all time
record stage Friday.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 25 at 3:01PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Tropical Storm In-fa (30W) is beginning to exit the northern Marshall
Islands as it moves northwest, currently passing near Bikini Atoll.
However, hazardous conditions continue across the region, with
scatterometry this morning showing fresh to strong southwest to west
winds across the northernmost islands and atolls of the RMI. Seas
will remain hazardous to small craft across the area through tonight
as In-fa moves away, due to elevated wind waves and west to
southwest swell, and inter-island travel is strongly discouraged.
Locally heavy showers may produce sudden, strong to near-gale
gusts, leading to locally dangerous conditions. These conditions will
diminish over the next few days as In-fa moves farther away.

For more information on Tropical Storm In-fa, please refer to
bulletins from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header
WTPN31 PGTW and from the National Weather Service under WMO header
WTPQ31 PGUM.

properties.description:

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 24 at 10:48PM MDT until October 24 at 11:30PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
SVREPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northeastern Hudspeth County in western Texas...

* Until 1130 PM MDT.

* At 1048 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 8 miles southeast
of Cornudas, moving northeast at 35 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage
to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Dell City, Cornudas, and Salt Flat.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has extended
the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Hudspeth County in western Texas...

* Until 1215 AM MDT.

* At 1044 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

deaths occur in vehicles.

Waveland, Nettles Island, Saint Lucie Nuclear Power Plant,
Hutchinson Island South, Sewall's Point, Hobe Sound Wildlife
Refuge, Ocean Breeze Park, Frederick Douglass Park, Hobe Sound
Beach, Walton, Jensen Beach, Port Salerno, Surfside Park, Fort
Pierce Ocean Park, Hobe Sound, Witham Field, Jupiter Island, Rio,
Fort Pierce Inlet and Pepper Beach Park.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, and heavy downpours. Boaters should seek
safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 24 at 10:23PM MDT until October 25 at 1:30AM MDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
FFWMAF

The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Eddy County in southeastern New Mexico...

* Until 130 AM MDT.

* At 1023 PM MDT, A trained weather spotter reported several inches
of standing water from the Charley White Draw over Highway 82 west
of Hope. Flash flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northwestern Eddy County.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

peaked and will gradually drop into Sunday. While water levels
